newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen aiming to activate B-share market.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen aiming to activate B-share market.

text.p: The Shenzhen Stock Exchange will continue to take steps to activate its B-share market, Zhao Wenqi, senior economist of the exchange, said on Tuesday.
The measures included improving regulation of B-share companies, requiring them to publish information more swiftly to increase their transparency, Zhao told a luncheon in Hong Kong.
"We will also increase the number of listed B-share companies with larger capitalisation," he said.
The exchange will also abide by the ban on Chinese investors buying B-shares, which are reserved for overseas investors, Zhao said. Regulations limit domestic investors to A-shares.
"If they (Chinese investors) already hold some B-shares, they can only sell in the market," the economist said.
Zhao said turnover on the Shenzhen B-share market in 1996 rose 987.45 percent from a year earlier, compared to a 1,209.45 percent increase in turnover value of the whole market.
Nine new B-share companies were listed last year, bringing the total number of listed B-shares to 43, he said.

Zhao said the Shenzhen market had started a study on the index futures but he declined to give details or a targetted launching date. Every new product needed to be approved by China Securities Regulatory Commission, he added.
